resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com says a Eureka city park. The story reports that claim only. A 2024 Northwest Montana Lookout Association completed-projects PDF, seen only in a search snippet, reportedly says the Tobacco Valley Museum; its cached text is garbled and could not be checked, so it is not quoted.
Both the 2024 newsletter and the village's own page place the tower at the Tobacco Valley Historical Village, so the current home is not in dispute.

notes_for_editor: The 1979 destination conflicts across sources: firelookout.com says a Eureka city park; the NWMT 2024 completed-projects PDF (search snippet only) says the Tobacco Valley Museum and last use in 1962. The cached PDF text is garbled and the grep found neither, so the editor should check that PDF by hand before publishing a sentence on it. The record name 'Roberts Mountain' comes from the FFLA list; the sources read call the lookout Roberts (Shorty's) and Roberts Lookout. The 2024 sign text names a local man called Arthur, whose name a creek, mountain and lookout reportedly bear; the link to the Roberts name is not established, so it is not used. The access level 'public' is inferred from the village being a displayed historic site; no hours were found. Budget: one WebSearch; about six distinct pages read, with the completed-projects PDF and the 2024 newsletter each grepped twice.
